title: Austin Funds 10 New Affordable Homes
summary:
*   Approved over $350,000 in zero-interest loans to build ten new single-family homes.
*   Provided financial assistance to ten first-time homebuyer families in the Guadalupe and Blackshear neighborhoods.
*   Supported local community development corporations in their efforts to expand affordable housing options.

BOARD OF DIRECTORS' MEETING
AUSTIN HOUSING FINANCE CORPORATION
SPECIAL CALLED MEETING MINUTES
THURSDAY, MARCH 27,2003
The Board of Directors of the Austin Housing Finance Corporation (AHFC) was convened on
Thursday, March 27, 2003, in the Hancock Building Board Room of the Lower Colorado River
Authority, 3700 Lake Austin Blvd. The following were the AHFC items considered by the Austin
Housing Finance Corporation's Board of Directors.
President Garcia called the meeting to order at 3:35 p.m.
AHFC-1 
Approve the minutes of the March 6, 2003 Board meeting of the Austin Housing Finance
Corporation.
The minutes for the Austin Housing Finance Corporation Special Called Meeting of
March 6, 2003 were approved on Board Member Dunkerley's motion, President
Garcia's second on a 7-0 vote.
AHFC-2 
Authorize the negotiation and execution of a 0% repayable Community Housing
Development Organization (CHDO) loan through the Acquisition and Development
Program in an amount not to exceed $146,000 to the Guadalupe Neighborhood
Development Corporation for hard costs associated with construction for four (4) new
single-family homes in the Guadalupe Neighborhood, and to provide principle buy-down
and closing cost assistance to the four first-time homebuyer families in the form of
deferred loans. (Funding is available in HOME grant funds allocated in the Fiscal Year
2002-03 Austin Housing Finance Corporation (AHFC) budget.)
The motion authorizing the negotiation and execution of a 0% repayable
Community Housing Development Organization loan was approved on Vice
President Goodman's motion, Board Member Wynn's second on a 7-0 vote.
AHFC- 3 
Authorize the negotiation and execution of a 0% repayable Community Housing
Development Organization (CHDO) loan through the Acquisition & Development
Program in an amount not to exceed $209,000 to the Blackshear Neighborhood
Development Corporation for hard costs associated with construction of six (6) new
single-family homes in the Blackshear neighborhood, and to provide principal buy-down
and closing cost assistance to the six first-time homebuyer families in the form of
deferred loans. (Funding is available in HOME grant funds allocated in the Fiscal Year
2002-2003 Austin Housing Finance Corporation (AHFC) budget.)
The motion authorizing the negotiation and execution of a 0% repayable Community
Housing Development Organization loan was approved on Vice President
Goodman's motion, Board Member Slusher's second on a 7-0 vote.
